learningObjective: Explain the design rationale for a stable, versioned IR at the framework-compiler boundary.

canonicalClaims.claim: StableHLO's design rationale is to decouple ML framework release cycles from compiler release cycles by providing a versioned operator set with forward/backward compatibility guarantees, avoiding an O(frameworks × compilers) integration matrix.
conditions: Both producers and consumers respect the versioning contract.
nonImplications: Does not imply bit-identical numerics across backends.
Does not imply frameworks stop needing their own capture tools.

misconceptions.claim: StableHLO guarantees bit-identical numerics across all frameworks and backends.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Spec provides semantics with defined tolerances; different backends may produce slightly different results within those.

misconceptions.claim: Frameworks that emit StableHLO no longer need graph-capture tools.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Capture (Dynamo/JAX tracer/tf.function) is orthogonal; StableHLO is the target IR.

misconceptions.claim: StableHLO's purpose is to enable Python-source-level optimizations at the compiler level.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It abstracts away from Python; the IR is a hardware-agnostic operator set.

misconceptions.claim: The stable contract eliminates the need for per-framework testing.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Framework-specific edge cases and lowering paths still require testing.

implementationFacts: Versioning: producer version + minimum compatible consumer version.
